pairs: Direxit opera eorum in manibus prophetæ sancti.
She directed their works in the hands of the holy prophet.
Iter fecerunt per deserta quæ non habitabantur,
They made a path through desolate areas, which were uninhabited,
et in locis desertis fixerunt casas.
and set up their homes in remote places.
Steterunt contra hostes,
They stood firm against the enemy,
et de inimicis se vindicaverunt.
and vindicated themselves from their adversaries.
Sitierunt,
They thirsted,
et invocaverunt te,
and they called upon you,
et data est illis aqua de petra altissima,
and water was given them out of the deepest rock,
et requies sitis de lapide duro.
and respite from thirst out of the hard stone.
Per quæ enim pœnas passi sunt inimici illorum a defectione potus sui, et in eis cum abundarent filii Israël lætati sunt:

For through water, their enemies had been punished, by the corruption of their drinking water; and so, among them, when the sons of Israel lacked the abundance they would have had, their enemies rejoiced;
per hæc,
yet through water,
cum illis deessent,
when they were in need,
bene cum illis actum est.
it turned out well for them.
Nam pro fonte quidem sempiterni fluminis,
For instead of a fountain, even everlasting in flow,
humanum sanguinem dedisti injustis.
you gave human blood to the unjust,
Qui cum minuerentur in traductione infantium occisorum,
and while they would be crushed into disgrace because of the murdering of infants,
dedisti illis abundantem aquam insperate,
you unexpectedly gave your own abundant water,
ostendens per sitim quæ tunc fuit,
revealing through the thirst,
quemadmodum tuos exaltares,
which occurred at that time,
et adversarios illorum necares.
how you would exalt your own and would kill their adversaries.
Cum enim tentati sunt,
For when they were being tested,
et quidem cum misericordia disciplinam accipientes,
and even when receiving merciful correction, they knew in what way,
scierunt quemadmodum cum ira judicati impii tormenta paterentur.
when your wrath judged the impious, they would suffer torments.
Hos quidem tamquam pater monens probasti;
For these, advising like a father, you approved;
illos autem tamquam durus rex interrogans condemnasti.
but the others, interrogating like a severe king, you condemned.
Absentes enim,
For whether absent
et præsentes,
or present,
similiter torquebantur.
they were tortured alike.
Duplex enim illos acceperat tædium et gemitus,
For they had received double:
cum memoria præteritorum.
weariness and groaning in the remembrance of things past.
Cum enim audirent per sua tormenta bene secum agi,
For when they paid attention to their punishments, to attend to their own benefit,
commemorati sunt Dominum,
they called to mind the Lord,
admirantes in finem exitus.
admiring the end result.
Quem enim in expositione prava projectum deriserunt,
For though they showed scorn by throwing out distorted statements,
in finem eventus mirati sunt,
in the end they were amazed at the result,
non similiter justis sitientes.
but this is not the same as thirsting for justice.
Pro cogitationibus autem insensatis iniquitatis illorum,
For according to the thinking of their irrational iniquity,
quod quidam errantes colebant mutos serpentes et bestias supervacuas,
because some, going astray, were worshiping mute serpents and worthless beasts,
immisisti illis multitudinem mutorum animalium in vindictam;
you sent upon them a multitude of mute beasts for vengeance,
ut scirent quia per quæ peccat quis,
so that they might know that by whatever things a man sins,
per hæc et torquetur.
by the same also is he tormented.
Non enim impossibilis erat omnipotens manus tua,
For it was not impossible for your all-powerful hand,
quæ creavit orbem terrarum ex materia invisa,
which created the world from unknown material,
immittere illis multitudinem ursorum,
to send forth upon them a multitude of bears,
aut audaces leones,
or fierce lions,
aut novi generis ira plenas ignotas bestias,
or, in anger, beasts of a new kind,
aut vaporem ignium spirantes,
massive and strange, either breathing out a fiery vapor,
aut fumi odorem proferentes,
or sending forth an odorous smoke,
aut horrendas ab oculis scintillas emittentes;
or shooting horrible sparks from their eyes;
quarum non solum læsura poterat illos exterminare,
whereby,
sed
not only wounds would be able to destroy them,
et aspectus per timorem occidere.
but also the very sight would kill them through fear.
Sed et sine his uno spiritu poterant occidi,
Yet,
persecutionem passi ab ipsis factis suis,
even without these,
et dispersi per spiritum virtutis tuæ:
they could have been killed with one breath,
sed omnia in mensura,
suffering persecution of their own making and being scattered by your spirit of virtue;
et numero et pondere disposuisti.
but you have ordered all things in size and number and weight.
Multum enim valere,
Though many are strong,
tibi soli supererat semper:
you alone always overcome.
et virtuti brachii tui quis resistet?
And who will withstand the strength of your arm?
Quoniam tamquam momentum stateræ,
For, like a tiny grain on a scale,
sic est ante te orbis terrarum,
just so is the world before you,
et tamquam gutta roris antelucani quæ descendit in terram.
and like a drop of dew before dawn, which descends upon the earth.
Sed misereris omnium,
But you are merciful to all,
quia omnia potes;
because you can do all,
et dissimulas peccata hominum, propter pœnitentiam.
and you dismiss the sins of man because of repentance.
Diligis enim omnia quæ sunt,
For you love all things that are,
et nihil odisti eorum quæ fecisti;
and you hate nothing of the things you have made;
nec enim odiens aliquid constituisti aut fecisti.
for you would not have created or established anything that you hated.
Quomodo autem posset aliquid permanere,
For how could anything endure,
nisi tu voluisses?
except by your will?
aut quod a te vocatum non esset conservaretur?
Or what, having been called by you not to exist, would be preserved?
Parcis autem omnibus,
Yet you spare all things,
quoniam tua sunt,
because they are yours,
Domine,
O Lord,
qui amas animas.
who loves souls.
